title: Trace Style Linting & Dashboard Metric Contracts — working draft
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic working draft for two related chunks of observability hygiene: a trace/span style and linting checklist (to be enforced via CI and a telemetry pre-commit hook) and a small set of metric/dashboard contract templates intended to reduce iteration and operator confusion during rollouts. Goal is to reduce oncall time-to-blame, prevent metric proliferation, and make dashboard panels predictable and cheap to query.

Scope and audience:
- Owners: eng-observability and service owners that onboard new models/services.
- Applies to: inference service layers (frontend proxy, router, model-worker), console instrumentation, private-deploy telemetry shims.
- Not in scope: external customer metrics (billing), long-term archival formats.

High-level constraints and principles:
1) Names are machine-parsable: use dot-separated tokens; include service, domain, metric, aggregation, unit when applicable. e.g. "serving.router.request.count.delta" or "serving.model.kvcache.hit_rate.pct_1m".
2) Keep cardinality budgets per-metric (default: <= 3 dynamic tags for high QPS metrics). If a metric needs >3 dynamic tags, escalate to eng-observability for evaluation.
3) Prefer derived dashboards over raw ad-hoc queries; provide canonical panel definitions in the repo.
4) Traces should be human-friendly at a glance: span names should describe action or API (not internal function names).

Metric contract template (copy this for any new metric):
- canonical_name: string (dot.delimited)
- owner: team/name
- description: short (1–2 sentences)
- intended_aggregation: count|rate|p50|p95|avg|sum|gauge
- unit: tokens|ms|requests|pct|bytes
- cardinality_budget: integer
- tags_allowed: list (max 6)
- alerting_intent: none|critical|warning
- dashboard_panel_slug: path/to/panel
- rollout_milestones: feature-flag, canary, general-availability

Example (copy-paste):
- canonical_name: serving.router.request.latency.p50.ms
- owner: eng-serving-runtime
- description: p50 end-to-end latency from API ingress to first token returned (excludes client network).
- intended_aggregation: p50
- unit: ms
- cardinality_budget: 2
- tags_allowed: [tenant_id, model_family]
- alerting_intent: warning
- dashboard_panel_slug: dashboards/latency/ingress-p50
- rollout_milestones: [feature-flag, canary]

Trace & span style guide (lint rules):
- Overall: prefer short actionable names, lowercase, hyphenated for multi-word e.g. "http:ingest.receive" or "model:kvcache.load-miss". Use prefixes: http:, rpc:, model:, cache:, routing:.
- Span name structure: <prefix>:<action> (optional target) e.g. "model:generate.step", "http:proxy.forward". Avoid file/path/function names.
- Key attributes (span tags) to always include if available: request_id, trace_phase (ingest|routing|generation|postprocess), model_name, model_version, tenant_id (hashed), sequence_length, input_tokens.
- Avoid PII: never include raw user text fields in attributes. For debugging only, use sampling + redaction pipelines.
- Duration vs timing: record both duration_ms and event timestamps for long-running spans (>2s).
- Span boundaries: keep spans coarse-grained for ops (<=5 spans in hot path) and use child internal spans for developer-level detail gated by debug sampling.

Trace linting CI rules (proposed):
1) No dynamically generated names (e.g., function pointers) — lint fails if non-whitelisted characters present.
2) Required attributes present (fail if missing request_id or trace_phase).
3) Cardinality check for tags — flag if more than allowed tag keys in a metric/span.
4) Deprecated metric/trace name scanner — warns if referencing a sunsetted canonical_name.
Implementation notes: integrate with telemetry-lint (repo linked above). Provide a pre-commit hook that runs a lightweight static check of span names in code + a test that validates metrics that CI can run.

Dashboard panel guidance and skeletons:
- Panel ID naming: dashboards/<domain>/<short-slug> (repo-backed).
- Preferred panel sizes: compact (single stat + sparkline) for high-cardinality metrics; 2x1 for distributions (latency histograms); 3x2 for cohort-exploration panels.
- Panel data windows: default 1h with quick options {5m, 15m, 1h, 6h, 24h}.
- Query cost guardrails: add a max-rows cap and enforce sampled traces for historical views. Use derived tables for expensive joins (e.g., join request metadata to model labels) and reference those tables in panels.
- Example panel template (latency p95):
  - Title: "Ingress p95 latency (tenant-weighted)"
  - Metric: serving.router.request.latency.p95.ms
  - Breakdown: model_family, region
  - Thresholds: warning at 200ms, critical at 500ms
  - Notes field: link to runbook + metric contract id

Alerting patterns:
- Alert types: immediate (critical), trend (rate of increase over baseline), noise-tolerant (multi-window confirmation).
- Use multi-window confirmation for p95 regressions: trigger if current p95 > baseline*1.25 AND absolute delta > 50ms sustained for 3 consecutive windows.
- Pager escalation: primary owner -> eng-observability -> SRE oncall. Attach runbook snippet and rollback checklist.

Sampling and trace budget:
- Sampling tiers:
  - always-sample: critical flows with high business impact (e.g., billing validation).
  - rate-sample-default: 0.5% of requests for high-QPS endpoints.
  - debug-sample: on-demand via dynamic sampling flags.
- Trace-retention tiers: hot (30d), warm (90d aggregated), cold (365d aggregated). Specific dashboard queries should reference the correct retention tier.

Rollout checklist (minimum):
- Create metric contract in telemetry-contracts repo (PR)
- Add span names to trace-style registry (yaml) + pass telemetry-lint
- Add dashboard panel skeleton and link from contract
- QA synthetic canary run for 24h with target traffic mix
- Enable sampling and verify trace links resolve in dev and canary

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we version metric contracts? (pro: explicit migrations; con: extra churn) — propose v1 semantics first.
- Enforcement model for tag cardinality: hard fail vs scheduled audit? (pending SLO impact analysis)
- How granular should per-tenant telemetry be in Dedicated vs Hosted (privacy & cost tradeoffs) — need privacy review from legal.

Short term action items (next 2 sprints):
- [Asha] Draft telemetry-lint rule set and open PR for CI integration (due 2025-03-10).
- [Claire] Prototype dashboard skeletons for latency/cost/kv-warmth panels (due 2025-03-17).
- [Evan] Build a sampling-demo flag and test on staging for trace retention flows (due 2025-03-12).
- [Ravi] Run a cardinality audit on top-50 metrics and report high offenders (due 2025-03-20).

Notes to self / working threads:
- Slack thread: #obs-telemetry for rapid feedback, reference message ts 1678912345.
- Related Confluence: OBS-123 (trace style guide), OBS-222 (dashboard panel library).
- GitHub: telemetry-lint repo (see linked PR for an example rule).

Appendix: quick lint checklist for devs (copy into PR templates)
- Does this change add a new metric? If yes, has a telemetry contract been added?
- Are span names human readable and prefixed?
- Are PII fields avoided in span attributes?
- Does the metric adhere to cardinality budget?
- Is there a dashboard skeleton or a TODO panel linked in the contract?
